summary.headline: PFS Q2 FY27 loan assets rose 25% QoQ to INR3,684 crores; gross Stage 3 fell to INR126 crores but net Stage 3 rose to about INR105 crores.
summary.overview: Loan assets returned to growth, rising to INR3,684 crores from INR2,946 crores QoQ, while sanctions (INR3,098 crores) and disbursements (INR1,595 crores) hit multi-year highs. Total income was INR114 crores and PAT INR44 crores, with interest spread up to 1.18%. Gross Stage 3 fell to INR126 crores from INR190 crores, though net Stage 3 rose to about INR105 crores because a Danu Wind Parks account was technically written off and Kundli Manesar slipped to NPA with a INR19 crore provision. Management framed the quarter as the start of a portfolio-rebuilding phase in which spreads may tighten for a few quarters.

financial_highlights.change: +25% QoQ from INR2,946 crores; first growth after 10 quarters
19-quarter high; highest in about 4 years per management
management said PAT was broadly flat vs Q1 after the Kundli Manesar provision
down from INR190 crores in Q1 FY27

financial_highlights.value: 10.45% yield vs 9.27% cost of borrowing (period average)

segments.name: Renewable energy and energy transition
segments.commentary: Renewable energy now about 45% of the loan book. Q2 sanctions of about INR3,000 crores span renewables, roads, digital infrastructure, CBG and operating thermal; management cited roughly 15 borrowers and tickets of INR50-500 crores.

segments.name: Asset quality (Stage 3)
segments.commentary: Three Stage 3 accounts: Kundli Manesar (EAD INR124 crores, INR19 crore provision, about 15%), Varam Bio (INR2.10 crores, fully provided), and Danu Wind Parks (technically written off, previously about 75% provided, now in IBC process).

segments.name: Stage 2
segments.commentary: Stage 2 net of provisions is INR114 crores, all related to IL&FS; INR65 crores already provided, leaving INR65 crores net.

guidance_outlook: Management targets net loan book of about INR5,000 crores by end-FY27 (reaching it before end-March per Dilip Srivastava); about INR2,500 crores of sanctioned but undisbursed portfolio is cited as support.
Full-year ROA budget is 4.16% per Sanjeev Kumar; CFO said full-year ROA should be above the 3.49% H1 level.
Scheduled repayments of about INR300 crores expected in H2 FY27, excluding unpredictable prepayments.
Spreads expected to tighten for a few quarters during portfolio-building phase; long-term NIM expected to drift lower but not below 2%, with equity leverage target of about 4-4.5x over 3-4 years.
Cost of borrowing expected to fall each quarter as balance sheet grows; management targets market-rate borrowing within a year.
Credit rating currently A; management plans to approach agencies for an upgrade, with a rating review expected next quarter.
capex_capacity: Sanctioned but undisbursed portfolio of about INR2,500 crores, held pending compliance or completion steps.
Average ticket size INR100-150 crores per account; management expects it to stay around INR150 crores or somewhat higher.
Average seasoning of the loan book about 4 years; no seasoning target for the next 6 months.
Liquidity: positive cumulative net cash flow across all ALM buckets; total available funding and HQLA about INR600 crores plus.
demand_pricing: Central Bank of India sanctioned INR200 crores (new lender); INR100 crores drawn in September; a second bank has given INR200 crores in-principle, formal sanction awaited.
Management said the INR50 crore to INR500 crore ticket range reflects opportunity and quality; DISCOMs remain an option but only at acceptable pricing.
Management said the book is granular relative to peers but infrastructure tickets must rise to access better developers.
Repayments in H1 were about INR248 crores, mainly prepayments by state utilities (DISCOMs) on 2-3 large cases.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q2 provision and why did gross Stage 3 fall while net Stage 3 rose?
qa_highlights.answer: Kundli Manesar (INR124 crores EAD, INR19 crore provision) slipped to NPA; Danu Wind Parks was technically written off after about 75% provisioning, which lowered gross but not net figures. Net Stage 3 was about INR105 crores per management.

qa_highlights.question: Expected loan book trajectory and disbursement pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets a net book of about INR5,000 crores by end-FY27; about INR2,500 crores of sanctioned, undisbursed portfolio supports this. Scheduled H2 repayments are about INR300 crores, with prepayments unpredictable.

qa_highlights.question: Spread and leverage outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: NIM expected to decline gradually as leverage rises, but not below 2%. Equity leverage target is about 4-4.5x after 3-4 years of growth. Cost of borrowing expected to fall within a year as rating improves.

qa_highlights.question: Danu recovery timing and mechanism?
qa_highlights.answer: Recovery is through IBC proceedings, pending admission hearings; management expects a substantial recovery but said it is too early to value it, with cash likely in the next financial year.

qa_highlights.question: Gross NPA reduction and 0% NPA target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a 0% NPA target is aspirational; it is possible to resolve the INR105 crore net NPA within the year, but the company will keep provisioning standard assets.

qa_highlights.question: Yield and cost on incremental lending?
qa_highlights.answer: Average yield was 10.45% vs 9.27% average cost of borrowing. Management declined to give incremental yield or marginal cost, citing that rates are fixed only at disbursement.

risks_watch: Net Stage 3 of about INR105 crores after the Kundli Manesar NPA and Danu write-off; Danu recovery depends on IBC admission and bidder interest and is likely in the next financial year.
Spread compression as the book grows and leverage rises; management guided that NIM will fall but stay at 2% or above.
Concentration: average ticket size of INR100-150 crores and about 15 borrowers in Q2 sanctions; renewable energy about 45% of the book.
Funding cost of 9.27% and reliance on new bank lines (Central Bank of India INR200 crores, another INR200 crores awaited).
Pending credit rating review, with management planning to approach agencies next quarter.
Unresolved questions on the divestment process; management declined to give timeline or stage. Shareholder requests for buyback and dividend were not committed to.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and funding momentum, but evasive on pricing and divestment: management declined to give incremental yield, marginal borrowing cost, the divestment stage, and buyback or dividend commitments, and it deflected the Danu write-off timing.
key_quotes: Our loan assets have moved to an upward trajectory after a gap of 10 quarters, reaching INR3,684 crores.
Give us a couple of quarters when you will find spread metrics tightening for a bit because we are in the portfolio building phase.
Were the thermal power wave to come back at any point in time, we will take calibrated kind of exposures to that.
Once it is materialized, the disbursements are taken, then only the rate can be fixed up.

growth.why: Management targets a net loan book of about INR5,000 crores by end-FY27, backed by about INR2,500 crores of sanctioned but undisbursed portfolio and Q2 sanctions of INR3,098 crores (36-quarter high), though no capacity additions are discussed and spreads are expected to tighten for a few quarters.
